To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

professional learning communities are most effective when: they are focused on the improvement of teaching and learning, they are supported by a strong and clear vision and values, they have a shared focus, they have a strong sense of collective responsibility, they are inclusive of all staff, they have a high level of participation, they are supported and led by the head teacher or senior leadership team, they have an appropriate level of structure and formality, and they are focused on student outcomes.
the effectiveness of professional learning communities can be construed at the level of the individual teacher, the level of the whole school, and the level of the wider school system.

professional learning communities (PLCs) are more likely to be effective when school leaders identify and lead the three aspects of effectiveness described in the study, and that these three aspects of PLC effectiveness (i.e. leadership, learning, and change) are interrelated, and therefore, school leaders need to be aware of the interconnections between them.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how professional learning communities can be identified and led in ways that promote effectiveness in terms of (1) the quality of the learning that takes place, (2) the impact of the learning on student outcomes, and (3) the extent to which professional learning communities are sustained over time.
identifying the characteristics of effective professional learning communities and the factors that lead to them being effective.
identifying and understanding what constitutes effective professional learning communities and how school leaders can lead them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
effective professional learning communities are those that are both internally and externally effective, in which all three types of effectiveness are present and working in concert with each other.
professional learning communities are effective when they are: (a) effective at the individual level; (b) effective at the organizational level; and (c) effective at the system level.
effective professional learning communities are those that have a clear sense of purpose, a strong and supportive culture, and a commitment to continuous improvement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
effective professional learning communities are those that are able to develop the capacity of teachers to work together to enhance the quality of teaching and learning in schools.

professional learning communities, when they are effective, can be powerful agents for change in schools and in classrooms, with the potential to transform teaching and learning for pupils and teachers alike.
school leadership teams should identify the most important aspects of their professional learning communities and then focus their attention on those that they can most influence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effectiveness of a professional learning community can be enhanced by the extent to which its members identify with it.

professional learning communities are not a "silver bullet," but that their potential to improve student outcomes is real, if school leaders take a strategic, long-term approach to their implementation.
the most effective professional learning communities are those where the three aspects of effectiveness (i.e., student learning, teacher learning, and teacher well-being) are mutually reinforcing.
